intro: Poland is a parliamentary republic and a member of the EU and NATO. It spends more on defence, compared with the size of its economy, than any other NATO member.

chapters.title: President and parliament
text: The president is elected directly for five years and can veto laws; Karol Nawrocki took office in 2025. The prime minister, chosen by parliament, leads the government; Donald Tusk became prime minister again in 2023. Parliament has two chambers, the Sejm with 460 members and the Senate with 100.

chapters.title: Debates
text: Between 2015 and 2023, changes to the courts by the then government led to a long dispute with the EU over the rule of law. Questions about abortion, the role of the church and judges remain hotly debated.

chapters.title: Symbols and the world
text: The flag is white over red, and the coat of arms shows a white eagle. Independence Day is 11 November and Constitution Day is 3 May.
Poland joined NATO in 1999 and the EU in 2004. Fearing Russia, it has built up one of the largest armies in Europe.

keyTerms.meaning: The lower house of Poland's parliament.
The principle that everyone, including the government, must follow the law, judged by independent courts.
